From e0f3b803d74277677697bdf5b5e4c28766cfbc93 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Richard Weinberger <richard@nod.at>
Date: Tue, 26 Oct 2010 14:21:13 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] um: fix global timer issue when using CONFIG_NO_HZ

commit 482db6df1746c4fa7d64a2441d4cb2610249c679 upstream.

This fixes a issue which was introduced by fe2cc53e ("uml: track and make
up lost ticks").

timeval_to_ns() returns long long and not int.  Due to that UML's timer
did not work properlt and caused timer freezes.

Signed-off-by: Richard Weinberger <richard@nod.at>
Acked-by: Pekka Enberg <penberg@kernel.org>
Cc: Jeff Dike <jdike@addtoit.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Paul Gortmaker <paul.gortmaker@windriver.com>

diff --git a/arch/um/os-Linux/time.c b/arch/um/os-Linux/time.c
index dec5678fc17..6e3359d6a83 100644
--- a/arch/um/os-Linux/time.c
+++ b/arch/um/os-Linux/time.c
@@ -60,7 +60,7 @@ static inline long long timeval_to_ns(const struct timeval *tv)
 long long disable_timer(void)
 {
 	struct itimerval time = ((struct itimerval) { { 0, 0 }, { 0, 0 } });
-	int remain, max = UM_NSEC_PER_SEC / UM_HZ;
+	long long remain, max = UM_NSEC_PER_SEC / UM_HZ;
 
 	if (setitimer(ITIMER_VIRTUAL, &time, &time) < 0)
 		printk(UM_KERN_ERR "disable_timer - setitimer failed, "
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/um/os-Linux/time.c`**
   - The type of the variable `remain` was changed from `int` to `long long` in the `disable_timer` function. This change ensures that the variable can hold larger values, which is necessary because the function `timeval_to_ns()` returns a `long long` type. 

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `arch/um/os-Linux/time.c` addresses a bug related to the handling of timer values in the User Mode Linux (UML) environment. By changing the type of `remain` to `long long`, the patch ensures that the timer calculations can accommodate the larger range of values returned by `timeval_to_ns()`, thus preventing timer freezes that were occurring due to improper handling of these values. This fix is directly related to the issue introduced by a previous commit that aimed to track and make up for lost ticks, indicating a dependency on the correct data type for proper timer functionality.

Based on the commit message, the root cause and the patch provided below, you need to:

1. explain how the bug occurs, including all code statements that are most likely to lead to the bug and why. 
2. explain how the bug is fixed, including code statements fixing the bug and why. 

You must include one or more code statements in point 1 and 2.
Code statements included in point 1 should be as brief as possible, only include the ones that are most related to the root cause and  the number of code statements may not exceed 3.


Here is the commit message:
um: fix global timer issue when using CONFIG_NO_HZ

commit 482db6df1746c4fa7d64a2441d4cb2610249c679 upstream.

This fixes a issue which was introduced by fe2cc53e ("uml: track and make
up lost ticks").

timeval_to_ns() returns long long and not int.  Due to that UML's timer
did not work properlt and caused timer freezes.

Signed-off-by: Richard Weinberger <richard@nod.at>
Acked-by: Pekka Enberg <penberg@kernel.org>
Cc: Jeff Dike <jdike@addtoit.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Paul Gortmaker <paul.gortmaker@windriver.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the `timeval_to_ns()` function returning a value of type `long long`, while the variable `remain` in the `disable_timer` function was declared as an `int`. This mismatch in data types led to improper handling of timer values, resulting in timer freezes in the User Mode Linux (UML) environment.

Here is the patch:
 
 long long disable_timer(void)
 {
 	struct itimerval time = ((struct itimerval) { { 0, 0 }, { 0, 0 } });
-	int remain, max = UM_NSEC_PER_SEC / UM_HZ;
+	long long remain, max = UM_NSEC_PER_SEC / UM_HZ;
 
 	if (setitimer(ITIMER_VIRTUAL, &time, &time) < 0)
 		printk(UM_KERN_ERR "disable_timer - setitimer failed, "
 		       "errno = %d\n", errno);
 
 	remain = timeval_to_ns(&time.it_value);
 	if (remain > max)
 		remain = max;
 
 	return remain;
 }

```c

remain = timeval_to_ns(&time.it_value);
```
Reason:
The variable `remain` is declared as an `int`, but the function `timeval_to_ns()` returns a `long long`. This type mismatch can lead to data loss or incorrect values being assigned to `remain`, causing improper handling of timer values and resulting in timer freezes.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
long long remain, max = UM_NSEC_PER_SEC / UM_HZ;
```
Reason:
Changing the declaration of `remain` from `int` to `long long` ensures that it can properly store the value returned by `timeval_to_ns()`, which prevents data loss and allows for correct handling of timer values, thus fixing the timer freeze issue in the User Mode Linux environment.
